reason: Executable design review found that allowing Version/Rollback to reproduce a historical project status in the same operation would duplicate authority already owned and exact-SHA-qualified by BOOK-SYSTEM-LIFECYCLE-TRANSITION-ENGINE-001.
binding_rule: Version/Rollback does not change Book project or unit lifecycle status during restore.

RESTORE_CONTENT is the executable restore behavior and preserves the current project lifecycle status while restoring exact governed content bindings from the historical target as a new successor state.

RESTORE_FULL_STATE is accepted only when the target historical project status already equals the current project status; otherwise it fails closed with FULL_STATE_RESTORE_REQUIRES_PRIOR_LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION.

When a desired historical content target requires a different workflow status, first obtain and commit the exact status transition through BOOK-SYSTEM-LIFECYCLE-TRANSITION-ENGINE-001, then submit the content restore against that new current parent identity.

Historical author approval, export freeze, publication status or publication authority is never reactivated by content restoration. Any required current author/export/publication authority must be separately re-established through its owning boundary.

compatibility.effect: Narrows Version/Rollback authority to match existing qualified lifecycle ownership; no prior exact-SHA evidence is broadened.

qualification_requirement: The Version/Rollback qualifier must prove fail-closed behavior when RESTORE_FULL_STATE would change workflow status and must prove RESTORE_CONTENT preserves current status.
qualification_effect: NONE until the changed Version/Rollback executable subject passes its own exact-SHA qualification.
